question.problem:
What is the solution to the equation $0.6y=-4.8?$

The solution is $y=$
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, we multiply both sides of the equation by $10$ to get rid of the decimals:

$$
\begin{aligned}0.6y & =-4.8 \\ 10\cdot (0.6y) & =10\cdot (-4.8) \\ 6y & =-48\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve the equation using the multiplication principle, as usual:

$$
\begin{aligned}6y & =-48 \\ \frac{6y}{6} & =\frac{-48}{6} \\ \frac{\cancel{6}y}{\cancel{6}} & =-8 \\ y & =-8\end{aligned}
$$
